terms.definition: A type that lists a fixed set of related choices, such as north, south, east and west.
terms.example: I made an enum for the screen states, so the code can only be loading, loaded or failed.

terms.definition: A fixed value, such as a string or a number, that is attached to each case of an enum when you declare it.
terms.example: I gave each case a string raw value, so it matches the name the server sends.

terms.definition: Extra data that you attach to an enum case when you create it, so each case can carry different details.
terms.example: The failed case has an associated value for the error, so we can show the right message.

Hi everyone, welcome to Day 8 of iOS Daily English!

Today we talk about enums in Swift:

Enum - a type that lists a fixed set of related choices, like north, south, east and west.
Raw Value - a fixed value, like a string or a number, attached to each case when you declare the enum.
Associated Value - extra data you attach to a case when you create it, so each case can carry different details.

Every example sentence is read twice, normal speed and then slow, so you can say it out loud with the voice.

dialogue.title: Whiteboard: the states of one screen

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, Jake. Our feed screen has three states on the whiteboard. What are they?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Loading, loaded, and failed. Right now I use three Bool variables.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three Bools can be true at the same time. Then the screen shows a spinner and an error together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That already happened in the beta. So what do you suggest?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use an enum. It lists a fixed set of choices, and only one can be active.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the enum can only be loading, loaded, or failed. Nothing else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, and Swift checks every case in a switch. If you forget one, you get an error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. Now the server sends a status as text, like active or banned.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then give the enum a raw value. Each case gets a string, like active equals the text active.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And we can create the enum from the server text with the raw value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Correct. That returns an optional, because the text might be unknown.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, but I also need the error message in the failed case. Can a raw value hold it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. A raw value is the same fixed value for each case. You need an associated value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, I mixed those up. An associated value is extra data you attach when you create the case.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Failed with an associated value of type Error, so each failure carries its own details.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And loaded can carry the list of posts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Then the view cannot show posts in the failed state.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I like that. An enum, a raw value for the server text, and an associated value for details.
I made an enum, so the screen is loading, loaded, or failed.
